content.section: 6.3.3. Summary of alternative antiplatelet strategies to reduce bleeding risk in the first 12 months after acute coronary syndrome
content.summary: Alternatives to the default 12 months of DAPT after ACS include shortening DAPT duration (e.g., to 1–3 or 3–6 months depending on bleeding vs ischaemic risk) and de-escalating from prasugrel/ticagrelor-based DAPT to clopidogrel-based DAPT. De-escalation of antiplatelet therapy within the first 30 days is not recommended, but de-escalation of P2Y12 receptor inhibitor therapy may be considered beyond 30 days to reduce bleeding risk. Abbreviation strategies followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy within the first 12 months post-ACS can be considered for patients who are event-free after 3–6 months and are not high ischaemic risk. For high-bleeding-risk (HBR) patients, aspirin or P2Y12 receptor inhibitor monotherapy after 1 month of DAPT may be considered. Evidence is limited by trial designs and selection of lower-risk populations; some trials cited included only East Asian populations.
recommendations: Consider shortening DAPT to 1–3 or 3–6 months depending on bleeding vs ischaemic risk.
Do not de-escalate antiplatelet therapy in the first 30 days routinely; consider de-escalation of P2Y12 therapy after 30 days if reducing bleeding risk is prioritized.
Prefer P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after abbreviated DAPT in event-free, non-high-ischaemic-risk patients (typically after 3–6 months).
For HBR patients, consider aspirin or P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after 1 month of DAPT.
trials_mentioned: HOST-REDUCE-POLYTECH-ACS (tested prasugrel dose de-escalation vs standard-dose)
content.trial_notes: The HOST-REDUCE-POLYTECH-ACS and TALOS-AMI trials mainly included East Asian populations; HOST-REDUCE-POLYTECH-ACS evaluated reducing prasugrel dose (5 mg vs 10 mg) after 1 month of DAPT.

genes.context: Page repeatedly refers to P2Y12 receptor inhibitor therapy as a central antiplatelet strategy (examples: '12-month potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based DAPT regimen', 'De-escalation of P2Y12 receptor inhibitor therapy may be considered', 'P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy within the first 12 months post-ACS', 'aspirin or P2Y12 receptor inhibitor monotherapy after 1 month of DAPT may be considered').
